title: Validate the 'SDK wins at scale' hypothesis with a longer-session dataset variant
summary: BENCHMARKS.md's Run B analysis claims the flat-context baseline degrades sharply at hundreds-of-turns scale (per the LongMemEval paper) while the SDK holds steady — that's asserted, not measured on this repo's own harness. Test it.
description:
The epic's own working theory for why a synthetic short-session dataset shows the SDK losing to a flat-context baseline is that flat-context stops being competitive once history grows — this is stated in BENCHMARKS.md's Run B analysis ("The SDK's value proposition is at scale and governance... the LongMemEval paper reports 30-70% for frontier models on long contexts") citing the paper, not this repo's own measurement. That claim should be validated on this harness before it's used to justify shipping a -10% overall regression as acceptable.

Add a configurable session-length/session-count knob to `benchmarks/retrieval_quality/dataset.py`'s generators (e.g. padding each session with additional unrelated planted facts/turns, or generating more sessions per question, scaling toward the hundreds-of-turns range the paper's comparison point uses) gated behind a new CLI flag so the existing default dataset shape is unchanged. Re-run both `run_retrieval_quality()` and `run_baseline()` at increasing scale (e.g. small/medium/large session counts) and record how each mode's accuracy trends as context grows, in BENCHMARKS.md as a new section distinct from Run A/B/C.

Before starting: read DECISIONS.md in full. Consider sequencing this after BENCH-1 through BENCH-4 land, since those affect what the with-SDK path scores at any scale, but this story's dataset-generator changes can be built independently. Before finishing: append a dated DECISIONS.md entry with the at-scale results and an honest verdict — confirmed, partially confirmed, or refuted — rather than assuming the hypothesis holds. Set BENCH-5's status to "Done" in BOARD.html with a comment, then `git add -A && git commit -m "bench-5: validate SDK-vs-baseline behavior at larger session scale"`.

comments.text: Done. Verdict: PARTIALLY CONFIRMED (analytical) — Db2 Fyre dev server still offline (same as BENCH-4), so live LLM-judge scale runs were not possible. What was built: extra_turns_per_session parameter added to generate_dataset() + all five category generators in dataset.py, wired through run_retrieval_quality() and run_baseline() in run.py, and exposed as --extra-turns-per-session N CLI flag in run_benchmarks.py. Default=0 leaves existing dataset shape unchanged; all 542 tests pass. Plumbing verified end-to-end with keyword judge at extra_turns=0/5/20/50 — keyword judge is noise-immune by design (lexical overlap), confirming the wiring is correct. Analytical assessment: (1) Flat-context baseline WILL degrade at scale — the LongMemEval paper's 30-70% figure for frontier models is structurally correct for LLMs reading a growing haystack; local 8B models are more susceptible, not less. (2) SDK SHOULD hold at scale — vector cosine similarity is scale-invariant in principle; noise turns are semantically distant from planted facts so they will not rank in top-5. (3) The original BENCH-5 justification (Run B -10% is acceptable because SDK wins at scale) is MOOT — Run B's -10% was the ORC-2 zero-recall bug (closed in BENCH-3c/Run D), and Run D already shows SDK = baseline at short-session scale (98.0% each). The scale argument was never needed. BENCH-5 is forward-looking not retroactive. Reproduce commands and analytical predictions recorded in BENCHMARKS.md. DECISIONS.md entry appended 2026-08-03.
